newsitem.title: GERMANY: Arbitration starts in German building wage talks.
newsitem.headline: Arbitration starts in German building wage talks.

text.p: Arbitration in talks over wages and conditions for around 1.3 million German construction sector workers got underway on Wednesday, but politicians and union leaders gave mixed views on the talks' likely outcome.

Heiner Geissler, a member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democratic party who has been chosen to arbitrate in the talks, said he was "not pessimistic". But IG Bau trade union chairman Klaus Wiesehuegel said his view wavered bewteen being "pessimistic and neutral".
Unions are, among other demands, calling for wage increases of 2.9 percent and continued full pay during sick leave.
The last round of talks broke down without conclusive agreement in early April, prompting the appointment of Geissler as an independent arbitrator.
